title: Butter Bean Hamin with Vegan Stuffed Cabbage
subtitle: slow-baked with herbs and olive oil
description: Butter beans slow-baked in olive oil with herbs, garlic and cherry tomatoes, finished with stuffed white cabbage leaves filled with caramelised onion and bread.

steps.text: Soak the butter beans overnight in plenty of water. For the stuffed cabbage, cut out the cabbage core with a knife (making a triangular opening) and separate the leaves. Blanch the leaves in a large pot of boiling salted water for about 2 minutes until partly soft, then move to ice water.

Heat the olive oil in a large pan over low heat. Add the finely chopped onions and fry for about 30 minutes until deeply golden. Meanwhile remove the crust from the bread and cut the white part into small cubes. Mix the bread with the fried onion and season with salt and pepper (finely chop any leftover cabbage leaves, sear briefly and add to the filling).

Lay a blanched cabbage leaf on the work surface and cut off the bottom of the thick central stem. Place 2 tablespoons of filling at the stem end, fold once forward, fold the sides to the centre and roll forward like a cigar. Arrange in a wide container and refrigerate overnight (or continue straight away).
Drain the beans, place in a large pot, add 2.5 litres of water and bring to the boil over high heat, skimming the foam. Cook for about 30 minutes, then remove from the heat.

Preheat the oven to 140°C. Transfer the beans with all their cooking water to an ovenproof dish. Season with salt and pepper, add the sliced onion, garlic, herbs, cherry tomatoes and chilli and mix to coat. Pour over enough olive oil to cover fully, forming a seal over the beans. Cover the dish and bake for 6-10 hours.

Carefully open the dish, nestle the stuffed cabbage leaves into the beans, cover and return to the oven. Raise the temperature to 200°C and bake for 1 hour. If you like, uncover for the end to brown the cabbage rolls slightly.
